correctness.rationale: All quantifiers are over integers n>=2 and all Poisson-binomial laws supported in 0..2n. Lattice geometry forces a unique rounded law under transport radius <2/3; direct binomial coefficients produce an identity 80(a1*a3-a2^2)=n^2(3n-2)(3n-1)[81(n-2)^3+279(n-2)^2+279(n-2)+41]>0. Known product-law log-concavity forbids such a Poisson-binomial distribution. A full 64-unit coupling to Bin(4,1/2) proves sharpness at n=2. At n=1 a real-rooted quadratic attains 1/3. An exact checker confirms 349 cases and the coupling, but the algebraic identity, not enumeration, proves the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Tang-Tang explicitly pose the lower-bound problem for rationally scaled binomials. The novel general-family obstruction fixes its optimal dimension-free lower constant (attained at six trials) and identifies a structural local log-concavity defect valid for every sample multiple of three. This is an exact natural parameter-wide fact; it does not require a solved matching upper bound to be valuable, and its novelty is not the already published numerical n=2 instance.
